subproblem.title: Currents on ℝ^P vanishing off a compact K ⊆ U are determined by their restrictions to U (cutoff argument, parent step 3(d))
subproblem.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let K ⊆ U be compact, and let X, Y ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) (domain univ) both vanish off K. If X⌞U = Y⌞U (X.restrictDomain (subset_univ U) = Y.restrictDomain (subset_univ U)), then X = Y. Conventions: ℝ^P = Euclid P and Hᵈ = μHE[d]. For D ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^d(D) = TestFormOn D d (smooth d-forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in D) and 𝒟_d(D) = GeometricCurrentOn D d; ∂X = X.boundary (∂X(ω) = X(dω)). For G ⊆ ℝ^P, M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum of ofReal(X(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟^d(D) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x; M(X) = X.mass = M_D(X). An IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in D is the contract structure IMRep D d; R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHᵈ(x); R represents X when X(ω) = R.action(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^d(D); μ_R = R.measure = (Hᵈ⌞M).withDensity θ; X is integer multiplicity (IM, IsIntegerMultiplicity X) if some IMRep in D represents it. For V ⊆ D, ι = testFormOnInclusion regards ω ∈ 𝒟^d(V) as an element of 𝒟^d(D) with the same underlying form, and X⌞V = X.restrictDomain (V ⊆ D) ∈ 𝒟_d(V) is given by X⌞V(ω) = X(ιω). X vanishes off a set K if X(ω) = 0 for every test form ω whose tsupport is disjoint from K.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)) (X Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) d), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) d, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d)) K → X ω = 0) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) d, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d)) K → Y ω = 0) → X.restrictDomain (subset_univ U) = Y.restrictDomain (subset_univ U) → X = Y
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3(d) of the parent proof. That step proves ∂Ǎ = Ž with a cutoff ζ ∈ C_c^∞(U) equal to 1 on an open V ⊇ K. Here the same cutoff argument is stated for two arbitrary currents vanishing off K and is carried out through the vanishing property instead of the integral representations.
1. Choice of the cutoff. Since K is compact, U is open and K ⊆ U, there is δ > 0 with C := cthickening δ K ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). C is closed, and compact because ℝ^P is proper (IsCompact.cthickening). Also K ⊆ thickening δ K (self_subset_thickening, using δ > 0), and thickening δ K is open and contained in C (isOpen_thickening, thickening_subset_cthickening), so K ⊆ interior C (interior_maximal). K is closed. Apply the smooth Urysohn lemma on the Hausdorff, σ-compact, finite-dimensional manifold ℝ^P: Mathlib's exists_contMDiffMap_one_nhds_of_subset_interior, with model modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (Euclid P) (written 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P) under open scoped Manifold, which the contract scope does not open) and order ⊤ : ℕ∞, built from a smooth partition of unity. It gives a smooth f : ℝ^P → ℝ with values in [0, 1] such that f = 1 on a neighbourhood of K and f(x) = 0 for x ∉ C. Let ζ := f. Then ζ is C^∞ as a map ℝ^P → ℝ (contMDiff_iff_contDiff). The support of ζ lies in the closed set C, so tsupport ζ ⊆ C ⊆ U (closure_minimal), and ζ has compact support, being supported in the compact set C. Since {x : ζ(x) = 1} is a neighbourhood of K, there is an open set V with K ⊆ V and ζ = 1 on V (mem_nhdsSet_iff_exists).
2. Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^d(ℝ^P) with underlying form w, and put η(x) := ζ(x)·w(x). Then η is smooth (ContDiff.smul) and tsupport η ⊆ tsupport ζ (tsupport_smul_subset_left). So η has compact support and tsupport η ⊆ C ⊆ U. Hence η defines a test form η_U ∈ 𝒟^d(U), and ιη_U ∈ 𝒟^d(ℝ^P) has underlying form η.
3. The test form ω − ιη_U ∈ 𝒟^d(ℝ^P) has underlying form x ↦ w(x) − ζ(x)w(x) = (1 − ζ(x))·w(x), which is 0 at every x ∈ V. So its support lies in the closed set ℝ^P ∖ V, and so does its tsupport (closure_minimal). Since K ⊆ V, its tsupport is disjoint from K.
4. X is linear and vanishes off K, so by step 3, X(ω) = X(ιη_U) + X(ω − ιη_U) = X(ιη_U). In the same way, Y(ω) = Y(ιη_U).
5. By the definition of restrictDomain and the hypothesis X⌞U = Y⌞U, X(ιη_U) = (X⌞U)(η_U) = (Y⌞U)(η_U) = Y(ιη_U). With step 4, X(ω) = Y(ω).
6. Since ω ∈ 𝒟^d(ℝ^P) was arbitrary, X = Y (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose δ > 0 with cthickening δ K ⊆ U, and by the smooth Urysohn lemma a smooth ζ: ℝ^P → [0, 1] with ζ = 1 on an open V ⊇ K and ζ = 0 off cthickening δ K; then ζ has compact support in U.
For ω ∈ 𝒟^d(ℝ^P), ζω is a test form supported in U, and ω − ζω vanishes on V, so its tsupport misses K.
Since X and Y vanish off K, X(ω) = X(ζω) = (X⌞U)(ζω) = (Y⌞U)(ζω) = Y(ζω) = Y(ω); conclude by extensionality.

audit.reason: The smooth cutoff exists with compact support in U and equals one on an open neighbourhood of K. Consequently the difference test form has topological support disjoint from K. Linearity and equality of restrictions prove equality for arbitrary currents; no IM hypothesis is needed.
